subject: Dedicated GPU pilot: short-term capacity commit and SLOs
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@starlithealth.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pilot: short-term capacity commit and SLOs

Hi team — looping in infra and commercial on a small pilot ask from Starlit Health. Key points: they want to run an alpha integration (NLP clinical-extraction models) for a 3-week window in mid-June. They expect predictable latency for 95th percentile around 120ms for 512-token runs and would like a short dedicated carveout to avoid queueing on shared pools.

Request from Starlit (Rajiv in cc):
- Dedicated pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for 2027-06-14 -> 2027-07-05 (3 weeks)
- Autoscale exception: allow burst to +25% above the pool floor for short spikes (5–10m)
- Temporary SLO addendum and billing terms for pilot (prefer capped monthly $)

What I need from you:
- Dev: feasibility and ops constraints (can we guarantee the capacity window and a controlled burst lane?)
- Karthik: commercial guardrails and what we can offer for price/credits
- Laura: leadership sign-off if this requires a carveout or SLA deviation
I've attached a quick pilot_capacity_sheet.xlsx with estimated token volumes and expected concurrency.

Next steps: can we get an initial feasibility note by EOD Tue? Rajiv — if dates shift please flag.

Thanks,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pilot_capacity_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@starlithealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pilot: short-term capacity commit and SLOs

On Sun, 09 May 2027 at 16:12, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi team — looping in infra and commercial on a small pilot ask from Starlit Health.

Thanks Kim — flagged to infra scheduling. Quick reality check and a proposed path:

Feasibility:
- We can reserve an 8-GPU carveout in Dedicated for the requested window, but it requires advance scheduling to avoid overlapping enterprise pilots and quarterly buffer commitments.
- Autoscaler exceptions are possible but need to be scoped: we can offer a timebound "burst lane" policy (pre-authorized short OOB capacity) for up to +25% sustained for 10 minutes, not continuous. Engineering needs a hard ceiling and a per-minute billing multiplier for burst.

Caveats / risks:
- If other enterprise carveouts are approved for the same region (us-west) that week, we may need to move the window +/- 72 hours or offer a smaller GPU count.
- GPU packing + KV cache warming means the first 2–4 hours of the window will have elevated latency; recommend a ramp period and a warmup script from the customer.

Suggested next steps (ops + legal + commercial):
1) Confirm exact UTC start/end times (not just dates).
2) Lock down a per-minute burst multiplier (I suggest 3x token rate for burst minutes) and add to SLA addendum.
3) Draft short-term addendum (attached sla-draft.docx) and run legal review.

I attached the SLA draft with placeholders (billing, burst multiplier, measurement window). If Karthik can confirm a pricing concession we can pre-authorize the capacity.

Happy to run a 30-min sync with Rajiv and the SREs tomorrow.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sla-draft.docx (Word doc, 18KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@starlithealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pilot: short-term capacity commit and SLOs

Agree with Dev's recommendations. Commercial notes:
- For a 3-week pilot we can offer a stepped credit: 50% credit on dev hours + 10% flat pilot credit on usage up to an agreed cap. We should not commit to long-term pricing in the addendum.
- I'll open Deal DL-2027-1142 in HubSpot and add the proposed concession terms; finance will need to sign off on the credit schedule.

To move faster:
- Rajiv, please confirm: 1) exact start/end timestamps in UTC, 2) expected concurrency (peak callers), 3) whether warmup traffic can be scheduled 24–48 hours earlier.
- Kimberly / Dev: if legal needs the SLA placeholders populated I can shepherd that; otherwise I need a firm ask by EOD Wed to lock pricing.

I can also offer a short "pilot safe-fallback" — route to a slightly cheaper compatible model if latency exceeds the SLO for two consecutive 5-minute windows. That reduces risk for capacity tightness.

Karthik
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@starlithealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pilot: short-term capacity commit and SLOs

Thanks all — I approve a limited exception under these conditions:
1) Timebox: strictly 2027-06-14 00:00 UTC -> 2027-07-05 23:59 UTC (72-hour float allowed if scheduling conflict)
2) Billing: pilot pricing + proposed credit schedule (Karthik) and per-minute burst multiplier (Dev) recorded in the SLA addendum. No retroactive price changes after the start date.
3) Fallback: enable the model fallback route Karthik suggested if two continuous 5-minute windows miss the 95th pct SLO.
4) Legal & Finance: finalize addendum and send as DocuSign addendum prior to the start date; no capacity will be held without signed addendum and a payment authorization.

Action items:
- Dev: prepare ops runbook (warmup script, monitoring playbook, emergency release plan) and post to the Drive folder linked above. Due Thu EOD.
- Karthik: create HubSpot deal and upload redlines to the Drive. Confirm credit approval with Finance. Due Wed EOD.
- Kim: confirm final UTC timestamps with Rajiv and confirm that Starlit will do warmup traffic.

I'll loop in Legal if we hit any unusual redlines. Good work moving quickly on this — let's keep it tight and avoid opening extra carveouts for the same week.

Laura Bennett
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
